messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: TRIGGERED -> gpu-oom-alert-usw2a (P1)
incident-bot: 12 OOM/CUDA alloc failures in last 5m on pool gpu-pool-usw2a. Error snippet: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY". Affected hosts: gpu-12a, gpu-12b, gpu-12c.
incident-bot: Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-oom. Playbook step: check kvcache evictions, node memory, and active model batch sizes.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident created: https://pagerduty.incidents/PD-99321 (assigned to eng-oncall)

Maya S: ack - I'm oncall, taking lead. pulling logs now.

Sam L: I see a big spike in kvcache eviction rate and PCIe memory alloc fails around 05:12 UTC. Logs show repeated "cublasAlloc failure" then OOM.

Maya S: running: kubectl -n redwood top node gpu-12a && kubectl -n redwood describe pod inference-xyz on gpu-12a; posting small snippet:
```
Node gpu-12a allocatable: 80Gi memory
Pod inference-xyz: memory 22Gi, cache 18Gi, status: OOMKilled x3
Kernel logs: cublasAlloc returned error (all zeros)
```

Maya S: Quick customer check: console shows increased 5xx (backend) and latency spike for route /v1/generate-acme. Ava, any support tickets?

Ava (support): Yup, ticket REDWD-7521 from AcmeCorp. ~30% requests failing with "internal error: runtime out" from 05:10-05:23. Escalated to eng.

Sam L: hypothesis: kvcache prefetch + large batch sizes caused memory fragmentation under sustained concurrent generations. Also seeing autoscaler spinning up new machines but they immediately OOM.

Maya S: mitigation plan: 1) reduce max_batch on live route 2) set pool to degraded (no new allocations) 3) evict and cordon noisy nodes 4) enable fallback to cpu-small model for affected routes. Doing 1 and 2 now.

Maya S: running internal CLI:
```
# reduce batch size for route
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate-acme --max-batch 8 --reason "mitigate OOM"
# mark pool degraded
redwoodctl pool update gpu-pool-usw2a --max-alloc 0 --state degraded --reason "OOM storm"
```

incident-bot: Action logged: route update and pool state change recorded.

Sam L: after the override, OOMs per minute dropped from 12 -> 2. kvcache evictions still high but stabilizing. Metrics: kernel.alloc.errors 12 -> 2 in 3m.

Maya S: I've cordoned gpu-12b and triggered graceful eviction of inference pods: kubectl drain gpu-12b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data. Pods moved to healthy nodes and cpu fallback for some heavy routes.

Ava (support): AcmeCorp update: failures dropped to ~8% now, they see degraded latency but serving mostly OK. I sent a brief note: "We're mitigating an infrastructure issue; short degradation expected; follow-up to come."

Sam L: still seeing a noisy pod pattern on gpu-12c: repeated allocation thrash from model 'gptx-13b-quant'. I'm going to pin that model to a dedicated isolate pool for now.

Sam L: command:
```
redwoodctl model isolate --model gptx-13b-quant --pool gpu-dedicated-iso --reason "stop noisy neighbor"
```

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Escalation -> Level 2 assigned to Ryan K.

Ryan K: taking level2. quick summary: OOM storm in us-west-2a caused by kvcache fragmentation + large batches + prefetch; mitigations applied: reduced batch, degraded pool, cordoned nodes, model isolation, cpu fallback. Current status: OOMs minimal, customer impact reduced.

Maya S: handoff notes for Ryan: logs aggregated at https://internal.redwood/logs/gpu-oom/3055554321/ ; kernel stack dumps under artifacts/gpu-oom-3055554321.tar.gz. Next steps: monitor for 30m, if error rate stays <=5% unassign degraded state and increase batch gradually. Consider kernel-driver backport for cuda driver 12.1 hotfix.

Ryan K: acknowledged. I'll monitor the alert channel and start post-incident notes draft. ETA for handback to ops-runbook summary in 20m.

ops-runbook: Reminder: after stabilization run the postmortem checklist: impact timeline, customer list, mitigation timeline, and RCA hypothesis. Link template: https://internal.redwood/postmortems/template

Maya S: marking incident as mitigated for immediate paging. Leaving pool in degraded for 45m. If no regressions, schedule maintenance window for driver patch.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: ALERT -> Status changed to Acknowledged by Maya S.

pagerduty: Note: If OOMs increase >5 per 10m we'll auto-escalate to infra-oncall.

Ryan K: handoff done — I'll take next 30m watch and draft the incident blurb for comms. If anyone finds recurring alloc traces, ping me @ryan.k. :thumbsup:

Maya S: thanks team. leaving the channel but monitoring.

Ava (support): I'll follow up with AcmeCorp with an incident update and the expected timeline for a permanent fix.

end of thread
